raw_response:
I will keep my full 8.0 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, because that fits my land, irrigation conditions, and my experience. I have farmed for 40 years, so I do not need to take unnecessary risks. For wheat, I will use improved seed rather than old traditional seed, keep fertilizer at a moderate but solid level, irrigate a few key times with my well, and use rotary tillage because it is efficient for my scale and labor. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I want stable yield and stronger performance after wheat, apply enough nitrogen with balanced phosphorus and potassium, irrigate in the important periods if rainfall is not enough, and continue with rotary tillage so turnover between crops stays fast. I will not manage for maximum input; I will manage for stable output, good grain filling, and labor efficiency on a small farm with two people.
